messages:
ana li: Quick idea for prefix ownership: switch from long-running leases to a small immutable manifest per-prefix range. Manifest holds epoch, owner, seq. Update is a CAS. Cuts down heartbeat noise for very hot prefixes. Curious if people see any immediate safety holes.

tom reed: Hmm. CAS-based manifest seems attractive but where does the truth live? etcd? a single manifest blob? We need to think about atomic split/merge updates.

ana li: typo: ana* :-) Yeah, backend options matter. Proposal sketch: single manifest_id per prefix_range. Manifest blob contains {epoch, owner_node, seq, tombstone}. All operations do read->CAS. For splits/merges we update the namespace manifest_id with a new blob that encodes new ranges atomically.

vika: How do we handle read-after-write for clients that hit caches? If manifest flips, cached KV entries might be stale.

ana li: include manifest_epoch in responses and cache entries. Clients can attach observed_epoch on requests; the server checks observed_epoch <= current_epoch. If mismatch, respond with 409-like error prompting client to refresh. Also consider a short grace period where both sides serve but with degraded qps to allow retries.

tom reed: In-flight writes are the hard part. If old owner accepted a write right before manifest commit, and new owner already started serving, we could lose ordering. Need a way to sequence or drain.

rahul: Two mitigation ideas: (1) require writes to carry epoch token and sequence; new owner rejects writes whose epoch < manifest. (2) implement a short drain window triggered by manifest commit where new owner stalls applying writes for X ms while awaiting old owner's acknowledgements or replayed WAL. Not ideal but bounded.

vika: We must not regress availability. If we block on old owner and old owner is down, rollout stalls. So fallback should be automatic: if we detect inability to drain, we fall back to lease-based ownership for that prefix for a configured TTL.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolling canary started for manifest-proto on canary-4, see pipeline https://ci.internal/reports/3757. Note: expect more coord-store ops initially.

ana li: Good. Another safety measure: monotonic per-prefix epoch counter persisted in manifest; never reuse epoch numbers. That helps reject zombie owners. Add tombstone_ts for GC.

tom reed: For split/merge atomicity, I prefer a single manifest_blob per topology chunk rather than per-prefix small records. Avoid multi-key CAS complexity by bundling affected keys under one manifest id. We can keep per-prefix view derived from that blob.

vika: Telemetry: contested_attempts, claim_latency, epoch_rotation_rate, dual_serve_detected. We need alerts if dual_serve_detected > 0.

rahul: I'll wire metrics; also propose a deterministic chaos test: two workers racing CAS plus simulated crash/restart and network partition. Assert: no two nodes accept new writes for same prefix at overlapping times. Also assert staleness bound for reads (e.g., clients see at most 200ms stale epoch after manifest commit).

ana li: Migration strategy: feature-flagged rollout. Initially only read-shard demarcation moves to manifests (eviction still lease-based). Then we flip write-path after observing metrics for N hours. Include operator commands for force-rollover and dump-manifest for debugging.

tom reed: Operator tooling is important. Add a CLI: rw-manifest describe <prefix> --show-history and rw-manifest force-roll <prefix> --to <node> --grace <ms>. Also add a safety knob to revert to leases per-prefix.

vika: GC: compaction job to drop tombstones after TTL, and ensure manifest blobs don't grow unbounded with history. Keep only last N entries for debugging.

rahul: Tests list: unit CAS race, integration split/merge atomicity, chaos crash during commit, partition between node and coord store, and long-tail latencies under heavy manifest churn. I'll start a harness in the infra repo.

ana li: I'll write the RFC outline: motivation, invariants, data model, migration plan, operator tools, testing plan. Add sequence diagrams for normal handoff, split, merge, and crash scenarios.

tom reed: One more nit: eviction interaction. If eviction relies on leases to determine residency, switching ownership primitive may impact eviction heuristics. We should decouple eviction decisions (hotness) from ownership manifests. Eviction bookkeeping can remain local and use manifest only for serving gating.

vika: Good point. Keep eviction policy local; manifest only claims serving authority. That reduces blast radius.

rahul: summary of ownership invariant to include in RFC: "Post-manifest-commit, exactly one node is permitted to accept new write traffic for a prefix at the committed epoch; any node accepting writes must have epoch == manifest_epoch." We'll codify checks and tests.

ana li: Thanks all. I'll post the draft later today. Ping me if you want to pair on the split/merge diagrams.

tom reed: thanks.

vika: :thumbsup:
